assessment:
Cast a black tutor at this table and three seats decide you are digging for the infinite. You are almost never digging for the infinite.

You draw that loop complete in 4.6% of games and 25.0% when a wish goes into it, so carry the ticket and never steer for it. Your default wish is a two-mana enchantment that turns a token into damage at three seats.

Buy that layer the moment it has not shown up. TOKEN -> DAMAGE is drawn in 52.5% of games and 73.2% with the tutors counted, so half your games ask you to go and get it — go and get it, and stop agonising over which converter is best.

Spend the second wish on the multiplier beside it. THE GO-WIDE KILL goes from 40.2% to 63.1% with a wish, which is the largest single move any card in this deck makes to any number on the sheet.

Three of your four wishes are blank cheques. Demonic Tutor and Diabolic Intent buy any card at two mana into your hand; Vampiric Tutor buys any card at one mana onto the top of your library.

The fourth is a different animal, and it is the one that decides games. Forerunner of the Legion is {2}{W} for a 2/2 Vampire Knight — a Vampire spell, so it mints an eminence token on the way down — and its search finds Vampires only and puts the card on TOP.

Read that as good news with a rule attached. It costs you your next draw rather than a card out of your hand, so cast it on a turn you wanted a body anyway and never on a turn you need an answer in hand.

Then stop asking it for the wrong thing. It cannot reach a single converter — Purphoros, God of the Forge is a God, Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call are enchantments, and Corpse Knight is a Zombie Knight. When the converter is missing, that is a Demonic or Diabolic job.

One more thing about Forerunner, and it should make you bolder. The goldfish prices three tutors as wildcards and does not price it at all, so every assisted figure on this page is a floor — cast it on curve rather than holding it for a perfect turn.

Your commander does not carry the early game and you should stop waiting on him. He is a median turn six and lands by then in 52.3% of games, so the wishes have to win the first five turns without him.

One structural fact governs every loop wish. Bloodthirsty Conqueror is half of both verified lines, stacks 004 and 006, so fetch toward the half you already hold and keep two doors instead of one.

He is also a 5/5 creature, which means every iteration hands the table an instant-speed removal window. Count their open mana first — then spend the wish happily.

tutors.notes: Two mana, any card, straight to hand — the workhorse, and the only wish that can hand you a two-drop you cast the same turn. Mean available mana is 4.005 on turn four, so plan it as Tutor-plus-a-two-drop on four and Tutor-plus-a-three-drop on five; anything more expensive means you are buying next turn, and you should say that to yourself before you cast it rather than after. Never ask it what your best card is. Ask which missing piece turns the board you already have into damage at three seats — mean bodies is 2.637 by turn four, so the board is sitting there waiting to be converted.

targets.scenario: Turn four. Edgar is still in the command zone, you have two or three bodies down and a doubler resolved, and nothing on the battlefield converts an entry into damage. Player 2 is the durdle seat on four lands. Player 3 has a 4/4 and is looking at you.
targets.why: Take the cheapest door into your actual plan and take it now. Two for the Tutor and two for Tremors is the whole of turn four at 4.005 mean mana, so cast both and pass with the layer already live. From then on every eminence token is one damage to each seat, three across the table per body, with no combat step and no blocker in the way. Pick Tremors over Warleader's Call and Purphoros here purely on cost — you want the layer this turn, not next turn.

citations.quote: Your cards should do something to all three seats or win the game

targets.scenario: Turn six or later. Anointed Procession and Mondrak, Glory Dominus are both on the battlefield, you hold a two-mana Vampire, and all three opponents are above 20 life. Nobody is attacking you because your board is 1/1s.
targets.why: Close it, because the arithmetic is already on the record. Stack 008 ran one {B}{B} Vampire through one-to-two-to-four eminence doubling as five Purphoros triggers — ten damage to each opponent off a single two-drop — so hold that two-drop until Purphoros lands, then cast it and watch the whole table take a Lava Axe. Deploy him into the control seat's held sweeper without flinching: he is indestructible and at this deck's devotion usually not even a creature. With both doublers already down you are exactly one wish from the half that pays, so spend it.

citations.quote: reach must scale (each-opponent drains, commander damage, damage doublers)

targets.scenario: You are behind and it is not close. The other go-wide seat has nine bodies to your four, your lords are dead, and you are the one being raced.
targets.why: Buy the reset only they pay for. Every non-Vampire creature gets -X/-X for your Vampire count, so keep four Vampires alive and their board eats -4/-4 while yours takes nothing. Count the collateral out loud first: Mondrak, Corpse Knight, Abzan Falconer and Ocelot Pride are not Vampires and go down with everyone else, so sequence those four after the Wrath rather than before. Five mana on top of the Tutor against 4.728 mean mana on turn five means you are buying for next turn — so cast Demonic on the turn you can spare it and keep the Wrath hidden until their board is worth the card.

targets.scenario: The wish nobody sees coming. The blue seat has held two untapped Islands every turn and countered the last two things anyone tried to resolve. You have a hand of Vampires and no way to make one stick.
targets.why: Fetching a land looks like a waste until you name what it buys. Choose Vampire and every Vampire creature spell you cast cannot be countered, which blanks their whole held plan for the rest of the game. Black is your short colour at 23 land sources against a 36-source yardstick, so play it the turn it arrives and let it fix as well. Hold one limitation in your head so it never surprises you: Cavern's coloured mana is spendable only on creature spells, so tap it for colourless or tap something else when you want Captivating Vampire's steal or Vito's lifelink pump.

citations.quote: ask which of the opponent's likely cards your permanent invalidates

tutors.notes: Two mana and a creature sacrificed as an additional cost — and eminence prints that currency for you, minting a 1/1 from the command zone on every Vampire spell you cast. Spend a token, never a lord. Look for two upgrades before you cast it: with Cordial Vampire out the sacrifice puts a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire you control, so cast Intent second and the cost becomes an anthem; and with a big Elenda, the Dusk Rose on a stalled board, SHE is the correct cost, because she dies into 1/1 lifelink Vampires equal to her power and any doubler doubles them. The one time Intent is wrong is the one time it looks right — when your only body is your only blocker, that body is not spare, and Demonic Tutor exists.

targets.scenario: Turn five or six. You have three or four bodies including a spare token, all four seats are developing, and nobody has committed removal yet. Your creatures are 1/1s and 2/2s and every opponent's blockers are bigger.
targets.why: Take the payoff that repays the cost twice. One damage to each opponent whenever a creature you control enters, plus a permanent +1/+1 to your whole board — so the token you sacrificed comes straight back as a point of power on everything you own. Take it over Impact Tremors here because your problem is two-sided: you need the entry damage AND you need the swarm to stop bouncing off blockers, and this is the only converter that does both. Three mana on top of the Tutor against 4.728 mean mana at turn five means you cast Intent and the Call on the same turn.

targets.scenario: A converter is already on the battlefield and undisturbed. You have four or more bodies, a Vampire in hand, and the table has spent its removal on each other.
targets.why: Double every future entry, and do it on a 4/4 body rather than a do-nothing enchantment. Stack 002 verified the doubling as one event and order-independent — one eminence trigger becomes two tokens, two doublers make four — so stop trying to sequence the doublers cleverly and just resolve them. Bank the neat part: Mondrak's indestructible ability sacrifices two other artifacts or creatures, exactly the tokens Intent spends, so count one pile of 1/1s for both costs. THE GO-WIDE KILL goes from 40.2% to 63.1% with a wish, and this fetch is what that second number is made of.

citations.quote: time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress

targets.scenario: Board stall. You have six or seven Vampires, Player 2 has a comparable board, the sweeper seat has held five mana open for two turns, and all three opponents are above 25 life.
targets.why: Stop being a token board. Every creature entering puts a +1/+1 counter on each creature you control, so one doubled eminence trigger grows your whole team twice, your 1/1s stop dying to -X/-X and they stop bouncing off blockers. Deploy it BEFORE the wrath and not after — counters are what keep a swarm out of Toxic Deluge range. Then remember Abzan Falconer is in the 99: every creature with a counter flies, and a stalled ground board is not stalled any more.

citations.quote: buy resilience instead of restraint where you can

targets.scenario: The wish nobody sees coming. Player 3 has resolved a Rhystic Study or a Ghostly Prison-style tax and the whole table is now playing their game. Your board is fine and your engine is stuck behind one enchantment.
targets.why: Exile any nonland permanent at instant speed, and pay the 3 life without thinking about it in a deck whose converters and lifelink tokens refill it. Respect this axis: an answer to a noncreature permanent is drawn in only 30.8% of games and 23.8% by turn six, so seven games in ten you have none — which means the moment a stax piece resolves, this is the wish, and you should not talk yourself into a converter instead. Fetch it and HOLD it. Let another seat spend theirs first, and use yours on the piece actually taxing you.

citations.quote: hold removal until the threat is pointed at you

tutors.notes: One mana, instant speed, 2 life, and the card lands on TOP rather than in your hand — so buy the answer to a threat you have PREDICTED and never one you are watching resolve. Cast it in the end step of the player right before you: you untap, draw it, and hold it a full rotation while the table watched you spend one mana and learned nothing. Protection turns up on its own in 68.1% of games, so plan on this wish covering the third of your games where it does not. Respect the 2 life at low totals, because Preacher of the Schism only draws you a card while you have the most life or are tied for it.

targets.scenario: The control seat has passed with four or more untapped mana for two full turn cycles and cast nothing. Your board is the widest at the table by a distance. It is the end step of the player before you.
targets.why: Buy the insurance before you need it, because an answer you never bought is not an answer. Your life total cannot change, you gain protection from everything, every permanent you control phases out — one card beats the sweeper, the targeted removal and the alpha strike aimed at you, so keep committing to the board instead of playing scared. Protection assembles on its own in 68.1% of games; spend this wish covering the other 31.9%, and spend it the moment their held mana becomes a pattern rather than an accident.

citations.quote: commit exactly as much as wins before it arrives, no further

targets.scenario: Bloodthirsty Conqueror has survived a full rotation on your battlefield and nobody killed him. You will have three mana next turn and the table is spent.
targets.fetch: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
targets.why: Take Vito every time this board exists — this is not a coin flip between the two halves. He is three mana against Sanguine Bond's five, he is a Vampire so he mints a token on the way down and every lord pumps him, and his lifelink pump turns your whole swarm into loop ignition. Stack 004 verified the pairing as a deterministic table-kill needing no further mana, so once both halves are down you need nothing else. THE SURVIVING INFINITE assembles in only 4.6% of games on its own — when you already hold one half, this wish is what converts the rest, so take the cheap half and keep mana up for Flawless Maneuver, which costs nothing while you control your commander.

citations.quote: assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: Edgar Markov is on the battlefield with seven attackers behind him and the alpha strike is next turn. Player 3 has four blockers and one untapped white source. It is the end step before your untap.
targets.why: With your commander out you choose BOTH modes, so plan the swing on that basis — flying, vigilance and double strike, plus lifelink, indestructible and protection from each colour. That is your board going over four blockers, connecting twice, surviving whatever they hold, and gaining you every point of it. Check your own battlefield before you count the damage, because every point gained is a live Vito or Bloodthirsty Conqueror trigger — and count the swing AFTER Edgar's attack trigger adds a +1/+1 counter to each Vampire, not before. Set the wish at their end step and let the table read one mana as a durdle.

citations.quote: sequence scary pieces after the table's removal is spent

targets.scenario: The wish of last resort, worth naming so you recognise it rather than fumble it. Vito has been exiled by a Swords to Plowshares, Bloodthirsty Conqueror is on your battlefield, and you still want the deterministic kill.
targets.why: Now, and only now, take Bond — with Vito gone it is the sole remaining partner, and stack 006 verified that pairing as a deterministic table-kill needing no further mana. Understand why it is last so you never reach for it early: five mana, no body, no creature type, no eminence trigger, no contribution to a single token. It buys no resilience either — Conqueror is still a creature and the loop still opens a removal window at every iteration — so count their open mana exactly as you would for the Vito line. Fetch Bond when the alternative is nothing, never when the alternative is Vito.

citations.quote: a Plan A and Plan B

tutors.notes: {2}{W} for a 2/2 Vampire Knight, so casting it mints an eminence token and every Vampire entering afterwards pumps a creature — cast it on a turn you wanted a body anyway and the search costs you nothing but your next draw. Its search is narrow and honest: a Vampire card, revealed, put on TOP of your library. Stop asking it for your conversion layer, because it cannot reach one card of it — Purphoros, God of the Forge is a God, Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call are enchantments, and Corpse Knight is a Zombie Knight. Never cast Vampiric Tutor and Forerunner on the same turn or the second one buries the first, and when Twilight Prophet has the city's blessing put Bloodthirsty Conqueror on top instead — that upkeep reveal drains each opponent for five and you keep the card.

targets.scenario: Turn four or five. You have four or five bodies from eminence tokens and cheap Vampires, no converter has shown up, and the table is at healthy life totals. You cast Forerunner as your play for the turn.
targets.why: Take it by default, because it is the only each-opponent payoff Forerunner can legally find. Every Vampire you control that attacks drains each seat for one and gains you one, and all of it resolves at declare-attackers — stack 003 put seven attackers on the record as seven separate triggers landing before blockers exist. So attack with everything and stop worrying about the block: a board of 1/1s becomes 7 damage to each opponent per turn. Your converter group sits at 52.5% drawn, so when Forerunner enters with that group still missing, take this card and start swinging.

targets.scenario: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or Sanguine Bond is already on your battlefield and has survived a rotation. Player 1 is tapped out, Player 2 has two untapped lands and has shown no instant-speed removal all game, Player 3 is low. You have {2}{W} and Forerunner in hand.
targets.why: This is the closing wish and the whole reason Forerunner earns its slot. Conqueror is half of both verified lines, stacks 004 and 006, and Forerunner is a fourth way to find him that the goldfish never counted — so treat the 25.0% assisted rate on THE SURVIVING INFINITE as a floor and act on a better number than the sheet shows. Fetch the half you are missing, never the half you hold, and keep both doors open. Count their open mana first, because the cost is your next draw plus a turn of exposure at five mana — then commit, knowing a 5/5 flying deathtouch body is a fine card on the nineteen games in twenty where the loop never happens.

citations.quote: essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck

targets.scenario: The behind fetch. Player 2's aristocrats deck is looping bodies out of its graveyard, your board got traded down to two creatures, and every removal spell you cast comes back at you two turns later.
targets.why: Take one card that stops the recursion and rebuilds you at the same time. Every nontoken creature an opponent loses is exiled instead of dying and you get a 2/2 Zombie for it, so keep pointing removal at that seat and let each answer become a body. Mean bodies is 2.637 at turn four and 4.103 at turn six — when you are under that curve, fetch the card that makes bodies out of their losses rather than a converter with nothing to convert. He is a 4/4 lifelink Vampire, so he mints a token, takes every lord pump and blocks for real while you rebuild, and yes, the Zombies still trigger Cathars' Crusade and every entry converter you own.

citations.quote: the deck's defense is speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers

targets.scenario: The wish nobody sees coming. Board stall at seven or more Vampires. Player 3 has a single enormous threat you cannot remove and cannot block profitably, and your removal is spent.
targets.why: Tap five untapped Vampires and take their creature permanently, for zero mana, at the cost of an attack you were not winning anyway. It becomes a Vampire in addition to its other types, so your lords pump it, Sanctum Seeker counts it as an attacking Vampire and Patchwork Banner's chosen type covers it. Stop letting the table forget this card is removal — and count the anthem too, because on a board of seven it is a seven-point swing before you steal anything. Attack the turn after with the stolen body and the stall is over.

citations.quote: one tax or pillow-fort effect can blank attack plans from three players at once

gaps: No wish here puts a permanent onto the battlefield, and none finds a card you can cast in response to something already on the stack. Demonic Tutor and Diabolic Intent are sorceries, Vampiric Tutor delivers to the top of your library, and Forerunner's search does the same — so sequence for one turn of exposure every time rather than pretending it is free.

Forerunner of the Legion finds Vampires and nothing else, which puts your entire conversion layer out of its reach: Purphoros, God of the Forge is a God, Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call are enchantments, and Corpse Knight is a Zombie Knight. When the converter is the missing piece, hand that job to Demonic or Diabolic and let Forerunner go and get the Vampire you actually wanted to draw.

The goldfish models three tutors as wildcards, not four — Forerunner is a restricted search and is priced nowhere in the simulation. Read every assisted figure as a floor: 73.2% for TOKEN -> DAMAGE, 63.1% for THE GO-WIDE KILL, 25.0% for THE SURVIVING INFINITE. Let that make you bolder about casting Forerunner on curve instead of holding it for a perfect turn.

Both verified loops run through Bloodthirsty Conqueror, a 5/5 creature, so there is no removal-proof assembly to wish for. Stacks 004 and 006 name the same cost: instant-speed creature removal in any iteration's priority window breaks the chain. Fetching the enchantment half buys the loop nothing it needs, so make the removal count before you commit rather than switching halves.

Four lines the strategic frame likes carry no stack yet — all four converters composing on one Vampire, Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubling a damage-sourced loss rather than a pure life loss, Corpse Knight igniting the Conqueror chain, and Cathars' Crusade into Abzan Falconer inside a single doubled entry. Do not spend a wish on arithmetic the checker has not run. Fetch the piece that is verified to pay and take the extra as a bonus.

A wish is a copy of a CARD, never a copy of a CLASS. Black runs 23 land sources against a 36-source yardstick, and Cavern of Souls is the only land in the 99 worth a wish — and its coloured mana casts creature spells only, so it will never pay for Captivating Vampire's activation or Vito's lifelink pump. Fix source counts in the 99; at the table, tutor the card and tap something else.
